First, note that the index $n$ starts from $3.$ However, it is still a geometric series because it is in the form $\sum a{r}^{n}.$ 

In this case, the first term is ${a}_{3},$ and so the sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of this geometric series is given by

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{3}}{1-r},\,|r|<1.
$$

For the first few terms, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3} & =\frac{25}{27}{(\frac{3}{5})}^{3}=\frac{25}{27}(\frac{27}{125})=\frac{1}{5} \\ {a}_{4} & =\frac{25}{27}{(\frac{3}{5})}^{4}=\frac{25}{27}(\frac{81}{625})=\frac{3}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

The common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{4}}{{a}_{3}}=\frac{(\frac{3}{25})}{(\frac{1}{5})}=\frac{3}{5}.
$$

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }\frac{25}{27}{(\frac{3}{5})}^{n} & =\frac{{a}_{3}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{5})}{(1-\frac{3}{5})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{5})}{(\frac{2}{5})} \\  & =(\frac{1}{5})\cdot \frac{5}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
